body.text: Sat, 15 Aug, 11:00 pm, Final score, AUS 198 & 284, BAN 426 & 1/57
South Africa-Australia Test series live updates: Bad light stops day one early
Bad light has stranded Matt Renshaw four runs shy of his first Test half-century in more than 3,500 days on day one of the opening Test between Australia and South Africa in Durban.
Play was stopped after just 65 overs were bowled on day one, with Renshaw unbeaten on 46 off 115 alongside captain Pat Cummins (33*).

If Renshaw can reach 50 it will be his first time past the milestone in Tests since March 2017, but that wait is nothing compared to Nic Maddinson, who was handed his first Test cap in a decade when the teams were announced on day one at Kingsmead.
The 34-year-old replaced Cameron Green in the XI but was elevated to open alongside Travis Head, sending Renshaw back down to the middle order.
Maddinson's first Test dig since 2016 lasted 33 balls and yielded no runs as he and Head (9) fell to leave Australia struggling after electing to bat.

Marnus Labuschagne (37) and Steve Smith (25) the first of the day's repair jobs before Labuschagne was trapped LBW by WIaan Mulder with the last ball before lunch, and Smith edged Marco Jansen to third slip three balls and 45 minutes later.
Renshaw walked to the crease at 4-84 and saw Alex Carey (14) and Beau Webster (4) come and go before finding a willing partner in Cummins, who made it through to an early stumps with him.
Look back at all the day one action in our live blog below, and check out all the stats in our ScoreCentre.

We'll be back tomorrow
This afternoon, actually, if we're going by AEDT.
Hopefully we can get in a full day's play, although I don't know if play can start any earlier than it did today.
Either way, ABC Sport will be here to bring you every moment.
Key Event
STUMPS HAS BEEN CALLED: Australia 8-187 (Renshaw 46*, Cummins 33*)
And that's it. Play ends some 40 minutes early today with barely 65 overs bowled.
It's a tough break for Matt Renshaw, who was looking good as he approached 50 and will have to start again tomorrow.
All told, another pretty poor day for Australia's batters, with one wicket consistently bringing two for the Proteas.

The Marnus Labuschagne-Steve Smith and Matt Renshaw-Pat Cummins partnerships showed fight, but that just rendered the former more frustrating by its premature end while the latter remains extant, albeit temporarily paused overnight.
The ground staff are prepping the covers
I think the end is nigh for today's play, team.
The ground staff are bringing the covers out. It doesn't exactly scream 'A resumption of play is imminent'.
Bowling fast under light
Hey Jon, do you reckon bowling very fast bouncers might not be a good idea when the light is in question? - Mike

- Mike
If you're the bowling team, it would be a very effective tactic I imagine.
Key Event
The players are going off for bad light
Only 65.2 overs have been bowled, but the thick cloud cover has prompted reserve umpire Stephen Harris to come out with the light meter, and the players are ordered off the field straight away.
It doesn't mean an end to the day's play for good, but we will need the clouds to get out of here if we want to see more cricket today.
What a shame for Matt Renshaw, a man with the most bizarre Test career, to be on the cusp of his first Test half-century in more than 3,500 days only to be sent from the field just four runs short.
66th over - Renshaw facing Nortje
Renshaw is 46 off 113.
The light meter is coming out. It does look very cloudy out there. And the players are heading off for bad light.
65th over - Keshav Maharaj gets a go
And again Matt Renshaw is straight on the sweep for an easy single.
Maharaj readjusts to the right-handed Cummins, but he's able to see it out.
64th over - Anrich Nortje comes in
Matt Renshaw is technically one strike away from his half-century.
Four more! Nortje goes short and Cummins rides the bounce, guiding it to third man. That's almost Cummins's primary scoring shot against real pace.
Nortje follows up with a proper bouncer that's just off line. And good thing too, because Pat Cummins didn't know much about it.
Four! Down leg this time. Nortje has Cummins jumping around, but he's working the angles for now.
And again Nortje responds with another bouncer. Cummins goes for the uppercut and misses out.
63rd over - Harmer again
Another drop and run from Renshaw. His running between the wickets has been excellent today.

Oh! A close call in about four ways for Cummins as he gets one down leg and tries to smack it away, but can't connect. He's almost chopped on, almost caught behind, almost caught at short leg, almost a boundary ...
Cummins adds a couple more with a well played sweep shot from a long way outside off.
62nd over - Anrich Nortje takes over from Wiaan Mulder
Can the extra pace unstick Matt Renshaw?
FOUR! Too full and straight to Renshaw and he whips in front of the leg gully.
Nortje follows up with the attempted yorker, but Renshaw chops down on it.
Excellent running from Renshaw as he drops to the off side and makes an early and clear call to take the single.
That's 50 up between this pair, just when the team needed it.
61st over - The game is waiting for another moment
It feels like the pressure is building on this Aussie pair and they can't quite break through it.
Four! Perfectly timed from Pat Cummins as Simon Harmer goes too full and too wide and gets driven through cover.
60th over - Mulder around the wicket
Renshaw is defending well, but not hunting for runs. In fairness, Mulder is bowling pretty tight lines.
Whoosh! He goes hunting for a big expansive drive and is incredibly lucky not to nick off as the ball seams away every so slightly. This is a real battle out there.
59th over - The spin stays in
Temba Bavuma likes what he sees from Simon Harmer as he tries to spin it away from Renshaw's outside edge, but Renshaw hits with the spin and takes a single through cover.
No major issues for Cummins either.
58th over - Mulder to Renshaw
He's around the wicket to left-handed Renshaw and still finding enough seam movement away to draw a false stroke outside off.

After a couple of miscues, Renshaw whips away through the leg side, finding the gap between mid-wicket and mid-on. Temba Bavuma tracks it down before the rope, so it's just three, but very nicely played.
57th over - The lights are taking effect
The cloud cover has arrived, the wind has whipped up and the artificial lights are starting to have an impact as Simon Harmer starts his 11th over.
A couple down leg almost yield results as Cummins nearly overbalances and falls out of his crease, but manages to keep his toe down in the end.

Top edged by Cummins on the sweep, and it sails over leg slip and out of reach for two runs. A lot of luck in that one, but credit the skipper for hitting towards where fielders aren't stationed, even if it took an unconventional route.
56th over - Mulder to Cummins
Four! Beautifully played by the Aussie skipper as Mulder strays too wide and Cummins opens the face and runs a ball past gully and to the rope.
He tries again, but makes better contact this time and hits it straight to point.
Both batters manage to work off their bodies and take a couple into the deep.
55th over - Simon Harmer keeps on spinning
And Pat Cummins gets low to guide a ball down to third man.
Cummins drives to mid-off and takes a quick single to end the over. So he will have to face the seamer, but Mulder is a little more comfortable than Nortje or Jansen.
54th over - Wiaan Mulder steams in after tea
And Matt Renshaw continues as he left off, leaving wide ones and working off his body into the leg side.
Good application from the rangy number five.
